ghs.assessment: The Japanese personifies a single abstract enemy: the void or nothingness. The English pluralizes it, uses plural agreement, and invents the proper collective name 'the Nihil.'
ghs.remedy: The enemy is the void.

rows.jp: 奴らはどこにでもいる。
rows.en: They're everywhere.

ghs.en: Those bastards are everywhere.

rows.jp: もう俺を包んでいる。
rows.en: They already surround me.

ghs.en: By now they are engulfing me.

rows.jp: このままでは俺は拡散して、希薄になってしまう。
rows.en: At this rate I will diffuse, growing thinner and thinner.

ghs.en: If I keep this up I will spread, and end up diluted.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that if the surrounding condition continues, Taichi will diffuse. The English implies that his own continuing behavior causes the danger.
ghs.remedy: If this keeps up

rows.jp: 階段を通過し、二年教室。
rows.en: Past the stairs. A second-year classroom.

ghs.en: I pass through the staircase to the Second Years' classroom.
ghs.assessment: Taichi goes via the stairs to a second-year classroom. A staircase is traversed along, not passed through, and the English invents a capitalized plural possessive name.
ghs.remedy: I take the stairs to a second-year classroom.

rows.jp: 冬子の個室。
rows.en: Touko's private room.

ghs.en: Touko's private room.

rows.jp: 周囲と隔絶された小さな要塞だった。
rows.en: A small fortress cut off from its surroundings.

ghs.en: A tiny fortress, separated from its surroundings.

rows.jp: けど主がいない。
rows.en: But its mistress is gone.

ghs.en: But its master is not here.
ghs.assessment: The fortress metaphor's 主 is its occupant or mistress, Touko. 'Master' introduces a masculine or owner-servant nuance.
ghs.remedy: its mistress

rows.jp: 強ばった意志とともに送還された。
rows.en: She was sent back with her rigid will.

ghs.en: She was sent back together with her stiff determination.

rows.jp: でも少しくらいいてくれてもいいじゃないか。
rows.en: But couldn't she at least be here for a little while?

ghs.en: But wouldn't it have been nice if she had stayed here for just a little more?
ghs.assessment: The Japanese wishes that she could have remained for at least a little while. 'A little more' presupposes an earlier additional stay that is not stated.
ghs.remedy: for at least a little while

rows.jp: 「ああああああっ、ああああああああッッッ！！」
rows.en: “Aaaaaaah, aaaaaaaaaahhh!!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "AAAAAAH, AAAAAAAAHHH!!!"

rows.jp: こけつまろびつ、門をまたぐ。
rows.en: Stumbling and sprawling, I cross the gate.

ghs.en: Running and falling and stumbling I fly across the gate.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that Taichi crosses the gate while stumbling and tumbling. The English invents flight and uses 'across' for passing a gate boundary.
ghs.remedy: I stumble and tumble through the gate.

rows.jp: 俺は街中を彷徨う。
rows.en: I wander the town.

ghs.en: I roam downtown,
ghs.assessment: 街中 means throughout the town or city. 'Downtown' restricts the search to a central commercial district.
ghs.remedy: through the town

rows.jp: 生者を捜して。
rows.en: Searching for the living.

ghs.en: in search of the living.

rows.jp: そもそも交差世界の残滓でしかないここに、もともと生者がいたのかどうか。
rows.en: Whether there had ever been any living person here to begin with, in this place that was merely the residue of crossed worlds.

ghs.en: Whether or not these dregs of a crossed world that these are, and nothing more, ever held the living in the first place.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese wonders whether living people ever existed in this place, which is only the residue of intersecting worlds. The English duplicates 'these,' leaves a relative clause without a predicate, and turns the local place into plural dregs as the container.
ghs.remedy: Did living people ever exist here in the first place, in a place that is only the residue of intersecting worlds?

highlights.text: Whether or not these dregs of a crossed world that these are, and nothing more, ever held the living in the first place.

rows.jp: けど捜さずにはいられない。
rows.en: Still, I can't stop searching.

ghs.en: But I cannot but search.

rows.jp: 人を求めずにはいられない。
rows.en: I can't stop seeking people.

ghs.en: I cannot but seek people.

rows.jp: 「あ……はぁ、はっ……ッ」
rows.en: “Ah……hah, hah……!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ah... haah, hah...!"

rows.jp: 一軒一軒、家を確かめていく。
rows.en: I check the houses one by one.

ghs.en: Building by building I examine the houses.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that he checks the houses one by one. The English adds a broader building-by-building count before narrowing the same objects back to houses.
ghs.remedy: I check the houses one by one.

highlights.text: Building by building I examine the houses.

rows.jp: 狂乱の半日。
rows.en: Half a day of frenzy.

ghs.en: For a half day of madness,

rows.jp: 俺は求め続けた。
rows.en: I kept searching.

ghs.en: I continued to seek.

rows.jp: 門の前で、へたる。
rows.en: I collapse in front of the gate.

ghs.en: In front of the gate I lose my strength.

rows.jp: 「……ったくなぁ……一人もいねー」
rows.en: “……Damn……not a soul.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...'mmit now... there's nobodyyy!"
ghs.assessment: The Japanese frustrated filler is roughly 'honestly' or 'damn.' The English creates the malformed clipped string ''mmit.'
ghs.remedy: damn it

rows.jp: どんだけ捜しても。
rows.en: No matter how hard I search.

ghs.en: Howevermuch whateverway I search,
ghs.assessment: The Japanese means 'no matter how hard I looked.' The English fuses 'however much' into one word and adds the nonexistent compound 'whateverway.'
ghs.remedy: No matter how hard I looked

rows.jp: もう誰もいないのだった。
rows.en: There is no one left.

ghs.en: there was no one anymore anywhere.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that nobody was left. The English stacks three negative scope expressions without idiomatic ordering.
ghs.remedy: there was no one left anywhere

rows.jp: けど疲労と引き替えに、少し、落ち着いた。
rows.en: But exhaustion buys me a little calm.

ghs.en: But in exchange for all this fatigue I had calmed down, just a bit.

rows.jp: 激しい運動をするため、脳が用いられたためだろうか？
rows.en: Was it because all that strenuous exercise put my brain to work?

ghs.en: It's because to make strenuous movements I needed to make use of the brain, right?
ghs.assessment: Taichi wonders whether he calmed down because strenuous exercise occupied or used his brain. The English says he deliberately needed his brain in order to produce movement and uses the count noun 'movements.'
ghs.remedy: Maybe because strenuous exercise occupied my brain?

highlights.text: to make strenuous movements I needed to make use of the brain

rows.en: “Ah.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ah."

rows.jp: そうだ。
rows.en: Yes.

ghs.en: That's right.

rows.jp: 突き動かされて、山に。
rows.en: Driven onward, I head for the mountain.

ghs.en: Stimulated, I head to the mountains.
ghs.assessment: 突き動かされて means driven or compelled by an inner impulse. 'Stimulated' suggests mere arousal or increased activity.
ghs.remedy: Driven by an impulse

rows.jp: 目を疑った。
rows.en: I cannot believe my eyes.

ghs.en: I couldn't believe my eyes.

rows.jp: なにもない？
rows.en: Nothing?

ghs.en: There's nothing here?

rows.jp: あのぼやけた不確定な理解不能空間は、きれいさっぱり消失していた。
rows.en: That blurred, indeterminate, incomprehensible space has vanished without a trace.

ghs.en: That blurry, indeterminably incomprehensible space had vanished without a trace.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese coordinates the space as blurry, indeterminate, and incomprehensible. The English turns 'indeterminate' into an adverb modifying incomprehensibility.
ghs.remedy: blurry, indeterminate, incomprehensible

rows.jp: 「……馬鹿な」
rows.en: “……Impossible.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...that's absurd."

rows.jp: 何千週と存在し続けたものじゃないのか？
rows.en: Hadn't it kept existing for thousands of weeks?

ghs.en: Hasn't this thing continued to exist for many thousands of weeks?

rows.jp: いや、万かも知れない。
rows.en: No. Perhaps tens of thousands.

ghs.en: Nah, it might even be tens of thousand.
ghs.assessment: The quantified count noun requires the plural 'thousands.'
ghs.remedy: tens of thousands

rows.jp: 「どうしてなくなるんだよ」
rows.en: “Why would it disappear?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Why has it gone now!"

rows.jp: 憤り。
rows.en: Indignation.

ghs.en: Resentment.
ghs.assessment: 憤り is immediate anger or indignation. 'Resentment' more often denotes a lingering grievance toward an agent.
ghs.remedy: Anger.

rows.jp: 絶望。
rows.en: Despair.

ghs.en: Desperation.
ghs.assessment: 絶望 is despair or hopelessness. 'Desperation' is an urgent drive to act under extreme pressure and does not preserve the loss of hope.
ghs.remedy: Despair.

rows.jp: 名状できない感情。
rows.en: An emotion beyond naming.

ghs.en:
Feelings I am incapable
of describing.

rows.jp: 痛み。
rows.en: Pain.

ghs.en: Pain.

rows.jp: 心からもたらされるものに束縛され、俺は立ちすくんだ。
rows.en: Bound by all that rises from my heart, I stand frozen.

ghs.en: Shackled by what is brought out from the bottom of my heart I stood, petrified.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that things produced by his heart bind him in place. The English adds 'the bottom of' and omits the comma required before the main clause.
ghs.remedy: Shackled by what my heart produced, I stood

highlights.text: from the bottom of my heart I stood

rows.jp: 「どうして……」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Why..."

rows.jp: 逃げたい。
rows.en: I want to escape.

ghs.en: I want to run away.

rows.jp: あたりまえの感情。
rows.en: An ordinary feeling.

ghs.en: An everyday emotion.
ghs.assessment: あたりまえ describes the wish to flee as a natural or entirely understandable emotion. 'Everyday' instead suggests frequency or ordinariness in daily life.
ghs.remedy: A natural emotion.

rows.jp: 必死で養った、俺のちっぽけな心にもそれはあった。
rows.en: Even my tiny heart, which I'd struggled so desperately to nurture, held that feeling.

ghs.en: It existed in this frantically cultivated, worthlessly tiny heart of mine as well.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese calls the heart tiny but says Taichi nurtured it desperately. The English changes desperate effort to frantic cultivation and adds the judgment that the heart is worthless.
ghs.remedy: the tiny heart I had desperately nurtured

rows.jp: みみ先輩、
rows.en: Mimi,

rows.jp: 友貴、
rows.en: Tomoki,

rows.jp: 霧、
rows.en: Kiri,

rows.jp: 美希、
rows.en: Miki,

rows.jp: 曜子ちゃん……。
rows.en: Yoko...

rows.jp: みんなことを、とても笑えない。
rows.en: I cannot bring myself to laugh at any of them.

ghs.en: I can't really laugh at all you guys.

rows.jp: けれどゲートはもうない。
rows.en: But the gate is gone.

ghs.en: However the gate is no more.

rows.jp: 帰りたくても帰れない。
rows.en: I can't go back, no matter how badly I want to.

ghs.en: I can't go home even if I want to go home.

rows.jp: 補正する『ずれ』はなくなったんだ。
rows.en: There is no more “misalignment” left to correct.

ghs.en: Correction: the 'shift' was no more.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that the discrepancy which might have been corrected no longer exists. The English turns 'correction' into an editorial label and merely says the shift is gone, obscuring its role as the object of correction.
ghs.remedy: There was no longer any 'discrepancy' left to correct.

rows.jp: 一人。
rows.en: Alone.

ghs.en: Alone.

rows.jp: 交差した世界。
rows.en: Crossed worlds.

ghs.en: In a world that has crossed,

rows.jp: 交差するのは一点で。
rows.en: They cross at a single point.

ghs.en: the crossing is at one single point.

rows.jp: それぞれの流れは、また続いていく。
rows.en: And each flow goes on.

ghs.en: Their respective flows are still continuing.

rows.jp: 「ああ……そうか」
rows.en: “Ah……I see.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ahhh... that's right."

rows.jp: 俺のいるこの虚無の街は……もう―――
rows.en: This city of nothingness where I am……has already―――

ghs.en: This town of nihility where I now live... is now---

rows.jp: 交差点を過ぎたんだ。
rows.en: Passed the cross-point.

ghs.en: Past its point of crossing.

rows.jp: 『Ｘ』の字を想定してみればわかる。
rows.en: Picture the letter “X.”

ghs.en: Understandable if looking at the very character "X".
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that the idea becomes clear if one imagines the shape of the letter X. The English supplies neither the person who understands nor an idiomatic conditional construction.
ghs.remedy: You can see it if you picture the letter X.

highlights.text: Understandable if looking at the very character "X".

rows.jp: 二本の棒。それぞれの流れ。
rows.en: Two bars. Two separate flows.

ghs.en: Two lines. Their respective flows continuing.

rows.jp: 一瞬の交差。だが流れは止まらないわけだ。
rows.en: A momentary crossing. But the flows do not stop.

ghs.en: The crossing is an instant. Yet the flows don't stop.

rows.jp: 俺はもう一本の流れに乗ったのか？
rows.en: Did I ride the other flow?

ghs.en: Did I ride a third flow here?
ghs.assessment: The passage has established two intersecting flows. もう一本 asks whether Taichi moved onto the other or another one, not a third flow.
ghs.remedy: Did I move onto the other flow?

rows.jp: いや……違うだろう。
rows.en: No……that can't be it.

ghs.en: Nah... gotta be something else.

rows.jp: 今の街は、残滓だ。
rows.en: This city is only residue now.

ghs.en: This town, now, is just the dregs.

rows.jp: 流れゆく二本の残像の交差点。
rows.en: The cross-point of two afterimages flowing onward.

ghs.en: The afterimage of the Cross Point of two continuing flows.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese describes the present town as the point where two flowing afterimages intersect. The English instead makes the Cross Point itself an afterimage and leaves an isolated noun phrase whose relations are unclear.
ghs.remedy: The intersection of two afterimages flowing onward.

highlights.text: The afterimage of the Cross Point of two continuing flows.

rows.jp: 『実』が過ぎ去り『虚』になったクロスポイント。
rows.en: A cross-point where the “Real” has passed away and become “Unreal.”

ghs.en: A Cross Point where Real has passed by and became Imaginary.
ghs.assessment: The coordinated perfect construction requires 'has become,' while the source describes the completed transition from real to unreal.
ghs.remedy: has passed by and become

rows.en: “...Haha.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...hahah."

rows.jp: 「ははは」
rows.en: “Ha ha ha.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Hahahah."

rows.jp: 「はははははははははははははっ」
rows.en: “Hahahahahahahahahahahahahaha!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Hahahahahahahahahahahahahah!"

rows.jp: この笑いは。
rows.en: This laughter.

ghs.en: This laugh is,

rows.jp: 祝福。
rows.en: A blessing.

ghs.en: a blessing.

rows.jp: ゲートが消えるまで、どれだけの時間がかかったのか知れない。
rows.en: There is no knowing how much time passed before the gate disappeared.

ghs.en: How much time it had passed before the gate had disappeared, I have no idea.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says he does not know how much time elapsed before the gate disappeared. The English gives impersonal 'time' an expletive 'it' and uses an unnecessary past perfect for the elapsed time.
ghs.remedy: How much time passed before the gate disappeared

highlights.text: How much time it had passed before the gate had disappeared

rows.jp: けっこう早かったのかも。
rows.en: Perhaps it happened fairly quickly.

ghs.en: Maybe it was kinda quick.

rows.jp: けど気の遠くなる年月だったのかも。
rows.en: Or perhaps it took a mind-numbing span of years.

ghs.en: But maybe it was a number of months and years that would boggle the mind.

rows.jp: どっちにしても、俺は堪え忍んだ。
rows.en: Either way, I endured.

ghs.en: Whichever it is, I will have to patiently endure this.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese states that, whichever duration was true, Taichi endured it. The English changes the completed endurance into a future obligation.
ghs.remedy: Either way, I endured it.

highlights.text: I will have to patiently endure this.

rows.jp: 逃げ場が遠のくほどの時を、闘い抜いた。
rows.en: I fought through enough time for every escape to recede beyond reach.

ghs.en: In times when the place of refuge grows farther, the struggle is to the bitter end.
ghs.assessment: Taichi says that he fought his way through a span of time so long that escape receded into the distance. The English makes this a general present-tense maxim, removes him as subject, and turns duration into plural occasions.
ghs.remedy: I fought through a stretch of time long enough for escape itself to recede into the distance.

highlights.text: In times when the place of refuge grows farther, the struggle is to the bitter end.

rows.jp: 勝った。
rows.en: I won.

ghs.en: I won.

rows.jp: それだけは確かじゃないか。
rows.en: That much is certain, isn't it?

ghs.en: That alone is certain, isn't it.

rows.jp: 「逃げ場がないなら……生きるしか……ないもんな……」
rows.en: “If there is no escape……then I have no choice……but to live……”

ghs.en: Taichi: "If I have no place of refuge... outside of living on... I've nothing... nothing..."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese means that if there is nowhere to run, he has no choice but to live. The English substitutes 'outside of living on,' leaves the construction without a coherent complement, and repeats an unsupported 'nothing.'
ghs.remedy: If there's nowhere to run... then I've got no choice... but to live...

highlights.text: If I have no place of refuge... outside of living on... I've nothing... nothing...

rows.jp: これでいい。
rows.en: This is fine.

ghs.en: That is good.

rows.jp: 「ざまあみろ、だ」
rows.en: “Serves you right.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Just dessert, yes."
ghs.assessment: ざまあみろ is the taunt 'serves you right,' not the food-related phrase 'just deserts'; the English additionally misspells that separate idiom as 'dessert.'
ghs.remedy: Serves you right.

rows.jp: トゥルー俺、ざまあみろ。
rows.en: Serves you right, True Me.

ghs.en: Just dessert, oh true self.
ghs.assessment: The repeated ざまあみろ is again a taunt addressed to the 'true me.' The English replaces it with a misspelled and contextually different idiom.
ghs.remedy: Serves you right, true me.

rows.jp: おまえは（俺は）ここで飼い殺し。
rows.en: You (I) get to rot here alive.

ghs.en: You shall (I shall) be kept here until you die.
Taichi: "......hahah."

rows.jp: 胸中、無数の感情が交錯し十字を描く。
rows.en: Within my breast, countless emotions intersect and trace a cross.

ghs.en: Within my chest, emotions without number blend in shape cruciform.

rows.jp: 編み上げられる、架空のタペストリー。
rows.en: An imaginary tapestry takes shape, woven from them.

ghs.en: An Air tapestry is being knit.
ghs.assessment: 架空 means imaginary or fictitious here. The English turns it into the capitalized noun 'Air,' and the progressive passive reads as a new action rather than the appositive image in the source.
ghs.remedy: An imaginary tapestry, woven together.

highlights.text: An Air tapestry is being knit.

rows.jp: それは彩なす情意のきらめき。
rows.en: A shimmer of emotions in all their colors.

ghs.en: That is the glittering sparkle of the varipatterned varicolor of emotions.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese describes a variegated shimmer of feeling. The English piles a redundant 'glittering sparkle' onto the malformed inventions 'varipatterned' and 'varicolor,' leaving no coherent English image.
ghs.remedy: the variegated shimmer of emotion

highlights.text: the glittering sparkle of the varipatterned varicolor of emotions

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ah, ah..."
Taichi: "AH---"

rows.jp: 叫ぶ。
rows.en: I scream.

ghs.en: Shouting.

rows.jp: 声のかぎりに。
rows.en: At the top of my lungs.

ghs.en: Up to the boundaries of voice.
ghs.assessment: 声のかぎり means with all the voice one has, conventionally 'at the top of one's lungs.' The English treats voice as a spatial territory with boundaries.
ghs.remedy: At the top of my lungs.

highlights.text: Up to the boundaries of voice.

rows.jp: 声帯を震わせて、空を引き裂くほどに。
rows.en: My vocal cords vibrating hard enough to tear the sky apart.

ghs.en: Vocal cords vibrate, enough to tear apart the sky.

rows.jp: それはもう声ではなかった。
rows.en: It is no longer a voice.

ghs.en: That's no longer voice.
ghs.assessment: The English lacks the article required for the count noun 'voice' and shifts the surrounding past narration into a contracted present.
ghs.remedy: It was no longer a voice.

rows.jp: 音。
rows.en: Sound.

ghs.en: It's noise.

rows.jp: 現象であり固有存在でもある俺の、物理的な軋みに他にならなかった。
rows.en: Nothing more than the physical creaking of me—a phenomenon and a singular existence.

ghs.en: It could be nothing else but the physical squeaking creak of the phenomenon that is my eigenexistence.

rows.jp: 視野がエフェクトで埋まる。
rows.en: My field of vision fills with effects.

ghs.en: My field of vision covers with special effects.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that visual effects fill his field of vision. The English makes the field of vision perform the transitive action 'covers' but supplies no object.
ghs.remedy: Visual effects fill my field of vision.

highlights.text: My field of vision covers with special effects.

rows.jp: 俺の意識を、かたちにした幻覚。
rows.en: A hallucination giving shape to my consciousness.

ghs.en: Hallucinations that took the shape of my consciousness.

rows.jp: レースのように美しいが、おどろおどろしい情念で編み上げられている。
rows.en: Beautiful as lace, yet woven from ominous passions.

ghs.en: Beautiful as if lace it was, yet, it was being knit out of hair-raisingly eerie emotions.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese compares the vision to beautiful lace while saying that disturbing passions compose it. The English inverts the comparison into ungrammatical word order and stacks incompatible adverbial forms.
ghs.remedy: Beautiful as lace, yet woven from disturbing passions.

highlights.text: Beautiful as if lace it was, yet, it was being knit out of hair-raisingly eerie emotions.

rows.jp: 揺れれば、垣間見える不浄の荒野。
rows.en: When it sways, I glimpse an unclean wasteland.

ghs.en: Shake it, and you can get a peephole's glimpse on a wasteland of impurities.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that when the lace-like vision sways, an unclean wilderness can be glimpsed through it. The English commands an unspecified 'you' to shake it, invents a peephole, and uses the wrong preposition after 'glimpse.'
ghs.remedy: When it sways, an unclean wilderness shows through in glimpses.

highlights.text: Shake it, and you can get a peephole's glimpse on a wasteland of impurities.

rows.jp: これが……俺か……。
rows.en: Is this……me……?

ghs.en: Is this... me...?

rows.jp: 目が、不可視をとらえている。
rows.en: My eyes apprehend the invisible.

ghs.en: The eyes are perceiving what cannot be seen.

rows.jp: 幻だと思う反面、真実だとも把握していた。
rows.en: Part of me thinks it an illusion; another part apprehends it as truth.

ghs.en: It's an illusion, I think, but on the other hand I also get that it is truth.
ghs.assessment: In this construction the count noun requires an article: he also understands that it is the truth.
ghs.remedy: it is the truth

rows.jp: ああ、これは。
rows.en: Ah. This is—

ghs.en: Ahhh, this is,

rows.jp: 変性意識(Aletered states)だ。
rows.en: An altered state of consciousness (altered states).

rows.jp: トランス。閃き。悟り。天啓。神秘体験。%Nそう呼ばれるもの。
rows.en: Trance. Insight. Enlightenment. Revelation. Mystical experience.%NWhat people call it.

rows.jp: 極まった精神が、その表層をして潜在意識と接続する現象。
rows.en: A phenomenon in which a mind pushed to its limit uses its surface layer to connect with the subconscious.

ghs.en: The Phenomenon where a soul reaches the extreme of an impasse, and that layer becomes connected to the subconscious.
ghs.assessment: The source describes a mind pushed to an extreme, whose surface connects with the subconscious. The English changes mind to soul, invents an impasse, and makes an unspecified layer the subject of the connection.
ghs.remedy: a mind pushed to its limit connects its surface layer to the subconscious

highlights.text: a soul reaches the extreme of an impasse, and that layer becomes connected

rows.jp: 俺は追い込まれた。
rows.en: I had been driven into a corner.

ghs.en: I had been driven into a corner,

rows.jp: ストレスによって。
rows.en: By stress.

ghs.en: by means of stress.
Hmmmmmm?

rows.jp: 電撃に打たれ佇む俺の、意識側面が疼いた。
rows.en: One side of my consciousness throbbed as I stood stunned, as though struck by lightning.

ghs.en: As I stood there stock-still struck by this electric shock, the side of my consciousness ached.

rows.jp: 側面にあるもの。
rows.en: Something along that side.

ghs.en: There is something on its side.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese fragment points to what exists as a facet or side of consciousness. The English instead locates an unspecified object beside another unspecified thing.
ghs.remedy: What lay along that facet.

highlights.text: There is something on its side.

rows.jp: それは錯綜する感情と距離を置く、沈着な知識の層。
rows.en: A calm layer of knowledge, removed from the tangle of emotion.

ghs.en: That is the layer of the precipitated knowledge laid to keep the complicated emotions at a distance.
ghs.assessment: 沈着 describes the layer as calm or composed; it does not mean chemically precipitated. The source says this calm layer of knowledge stands apart from tangled emotions, not that someone laid it down in order to keep them away.
ghs.remedy: a calm layer of knowledge that stands apart from the tangled emotions

highlights.text: the layer of the precipitated knowledge laid to keep the complicated emotions at a distance

rows.jp: 該博な意識は告げる。

ghs.en: I cannot control the amplitude of the vibration of my heart.

highlights.text: the amplitude of the vibration of my heart

highlights.text: So as to cover with muddy water the sewage being blown out.

rows.jp: 周囲に広がる理性世界に淘汰されないように。

rows.jp: そして。

ghs.en: And then,

rows.jp: ちっぽけだと思っていた自分の心に、なんてものが秘められていたのだろう。

ghs.en: This heart of mine I thought so tiny, yet what a thing was kept hidden within.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese marvels at what had lain hidden in the heart he thought insignificant. The English front-loads the object without a relative marker and joins an exclamation to it with a coordination that never forms a complete sentence.

highlights.text: This heart of mine I thought so tiny, yet what a thing was kept hidden within.

rows.jp: 人捜しの長い旅に疲れ果て死ぬとき、はじめて振り返ると捜し人が無言でついてきていて、にっこりとほほえみかけてきたような。
rows.en: As though, exhausted and dying at the end of a long journey in search of someone, I turned back at last and found the person I sought had followed me in silence all along, smiling at me.

ghs.en: It's as if you're dead exhausted after a long voyage in search of someone, and then the very first time you turn around there the person you were looking for was, wordlessly following you, grinning into a smile.
ghs.assessment: The source likens the feeling to reaching death exhausted by a long search, only then looking back and finding the sought person silently following and smiling. 'Dead exhausted' turns actual dying into an intensifier, the tense shifts from present 'you turn' to past 'was,' and 'grinning into a smile' distorts the gentle smile.
ghs.remedy: As if, when I finally died exhausted from a long journey searching for someone, I looked back for the first time and found them following silently behind me, smiling.

highlights.text: It's as if you're dead exhausted after a long voyage in search of someone, and then the very first time you turn around there the person you were looking for was, wordlessly following you, grinning into a smile.

rows.jp: 生後数ヶ月、中脳皮質系から視覚皮質に神経系が切り替わり、外界に適するための末梢機能が発達する時期。
rows.en: A few months after birth, the neural system shifts from the midbrain-cortical system to the visual cortex, and peripheral functions develop to adapt to the outside world.

ghs.en:
A few months after birth, the central nervous
system switches over completely from the
mesocortical pathways to the visual cortex,
a period of time taken for the development of
peripheral functions suitable for the outside
world.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese describes a developmental period when neural processing switches from a midbrain-cortical system to the visual cortex and peripheral functions develop for adaptation to the outside world. The English changes the subject to the entire central nervous system, adds 'completely,' and makes the period itself something 'taken for' development.
ghs.remedy: the neural system shifts from the midbrain-cortical system to the visual cortex, while peripheral functions develop to adapt the infant to the outside world

highlights.text:
the central nervous
system switches over completely from the
mesocortical pathways to the visual cortex,
a period of time taken for the development of
peripheral functions suitable for the outside
world

rows.jp: 俺は闇の中、無言で母を求め続けた。
rows.en: In the darkness, I kept silently seeking Mother.

ghs.en:
Inside the darkness I, wordlessly, kept
seeking mom.

rows.jp: それは肉体の変化を招いた。
rows.en: That brought about a change in my body.

ghs.en: That beckoned a physical mutation.
ghs.assessment: 招いた means that the sustained effort caused a bodily change. 'Beckoned' suggests inviting something to approach, while 'mutation' adds a genetic sense absent from the general 肉体の変化.
ghs.remedy: caused a physical change

rows.jp: 母は若く恐怖の虜で、知識を持たなかった。
rows.en: Mother was young, captive to fear, and had no knowledge of it.

ghs.en:
Mom was a youthful prisoner of fear, so she
did not possess knowledge.
ghs.assessment: The source coordinates three conditions: she was young, captive to fear, and lacked knowledge. The English makes fear the cause of her ignorance and uses the abstract possession phrase 'possess knowledge.'
ghs.remedy: young, captive to fear, and without the knowledge to understand

highlights.text:
a youthful prisoner of fear, so she
did not possess knowledge

rows.jp: 最適化されていくはずの桿体(かんたい)細胞と錐体(すいたい)細胞は、この時期、宿主を夜行性と認知した。
rows.en: During this period, the rod and cone cells that should have been optimizing themselves recognized their host as nocturnal.

ghs.en:
The rod cells and the cone cells, likely
undergoing optimization had, at that time,
acknowledged their host as a creature of
the night,

rows.jp: 桿状体(かんじょうたい)細胞が増加し、分布を決める。
rows.en: Rod cells proliferated, determining their distribution.

ghs.en:
deciding to increase the amount of the rod-shaped
cells distributed.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that rod cells increased and established their distribution. The English makes the cells consciously decide to increase an 'amount' and collapses the two physiological developments into one modifier.
ghs.remedy: The rod cells increased and established their distribution.

highlights.text:
deciding to increase the amount of the rod-shaped
cells distributed

rows.jp: 網膜(もうまく)周辺の未分化細胞が、擬似的な輝膜(こうまく)を形成した。
rows.en: Undifferentiated cells around the retina formed a pseudo-tapetum.

ghs.en:
The unspecialized cells around the retina
create a pseudo-tapetum lucidum.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese describes a structure that formed during the past developmental change. The English shifts the formation into present tense.
ghs.remedy: formed a pseudo-tapetum lucidum

rows.jp: エラーの重複か、硝子体(ガラスたい)と同化しようと透明度を失い損ねた細胞たちか。
rows.en: Perhaps errors compounded. Or perhaps cells, trying to assimilate with the vitreous body, failed to lose their transparency.

ghs.en:
Overlapping errors, maybe, or the cellettes
failing to lose their transparency as they
merge into the glassy body, maybe.
ghs.assessment: The source proposes cells that, while attempting to assimilate with the vitreous body, failed to lose their transparency. The English invents 'cellettes,' mistranslates the anatomical vitreous body as 'glassy body,' and states that merging actually occurred rather than was attempted.
ghs.remedy: cells that failed to lose their transparency while trying to assimilate with the vitreous body

highlights.text:
the cellettes
failing to lose their transparency as they
merge into the glassy body

rows.jp: それはわからない。
rows.en: I do not know.

ghs.en: What it was, I have no idea.

rows.jp: 結果として、瞳に入った光を、反射し細胞に二度重ねる構造を有した。
rows.en: The result was a structure that reflected light entering the pupil, causing it to strike the cells twice.

ghs.en:
The result being that I was endowed with
a structure where the light entering my
pupils would be twice overlapped on the
reflective cells.
ghs.assessment: The resulting structure reflects incoming light so that it passes over the receptor cells twice. The English instead makes the cells reflective and says the light is 'overlapped' on them twice.
ghs.remedy: light entering my pupils was reflected across the cells a second time

highlights.text:
the light entering my
pupils would be twice overlapped on the
reflective cells

rows.jp: 構造的には猫や犬と同一のものだ。
rows.en: Structurally, it was the same thing found in cats and dogs.

ghs.en:
Structurally speaking, it is identical to what
dogs and cats have.

rows.jp: またこの目は、静止物より動くものに敏感だった。
rows.en: These eyes were also more sensitive to moving things than to still ones.

ghs.en:
Also, these eyes had higher sensitivity
for things moving than ones still.
ghs.assessment: The comparison requires sensitivity 'to' moving things and an idiomatic contrast with stationary ones.
ghs.remedy: more sensitive to moving things than to stationary ones

highlights.text:
higher sensitivity
for things moving than ones still

rows.jp: 猫が小さな虫を玩ぶよう、俺もまた……。
rows.en: As a cat plays with a tiny insect, so too did I……

ghs.en:
As a cat plays around with tiny insects,
I, myself...

rows.jp: 闇の中、母は俺に何度もキスをした。
rows.en: In the darkness, Mother kissed me again and again.

ghs.en:
In the heart of the night, mom had kissed me
so many times.
ghs.assessment: 闇の中 is physical darkness in the recalled setting, not the temporal 'heart of the night.' The English also shifts the simple past into past perfect and adds the intensifier 'so.'
ghs.remedy: In the darkness, Mom kissed me again and again.

highlights.text:
In the heart of the night, mom had kissed me
so many times.

rows.jp: 俺はどんな影響を受けたんだろう？
rows.en: What effect did that have on me?

ghs.en:
What kind of influence could I have gotten
from that?
ghs.assessment: English ordinarily asks what effect something had, not what kind of influence a person 'got.'
ghs.remedy: effect did that have on me

rows.jp: 潜在意識の黒い奔流(ほんりゅう)から抽出できる記憶は、それだけだった。
rows.en: That was all the memory I could extract from the black torrent of my subconscious.

ghs.en:
The memories that can be extracted from the dark
rushing torrent of the subconscious were those,
no more.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that this was all the memory he could extract from the subconscious torrent. The English mismatches plural present 'can be' with past 'were,' uses an unexplained plural 'those,' and separates 'no more' from the quantity it limits.
ghs.remedy: That was all the memory I could extract from the black torrent of my subconscious.

highlights.text: The memories that can be extracted

rows.jp: そうだ。
rows.en: Yes.

ghs.en: Right.

rows.jp: 母は死んだ。
rows.en: Mother died.

ghs.en: Mom had died.

rows.jp: あのあと、死んだんだろう。
rows.en: She must have died after that.

ghs.en: She had died after that, I'm sure.
ghs.assessment: だろう marks inference, roughly 'probably' or 'I suppose.' 'I'm sure' makes the conclusion substantially more certain, and past perfect is unnecessary in the immediate sequence.
ghs.remedy: She probably died after that.

highlights.text: She had died after that, I'm sure.

rows.jp: だから俺は、支倉に預けられて。
rows.en: And so I was entrusted to Hasekura.

ghs.en: That is why I was put into custody of the Hasekuras.

rows.jp: ……今に繋がる。
rows.en: ……Which leads to now.

ghs.en: ...which leads to now.

rows.jp: じゃあ……俺が見ていたあの七香は？
rows.en: Then……what about the Nanaka I had been seeing?

ghs.en: Well... what is the Nanaka that I have been seeing?
ghs.assessment: The Japanese asks who or what the Nanaka he had seen was. The English uses an article before a personal name, mixes present 'is' with present perfect progressive, and describes an apparent person as a thing without framing the question idiomatically.
ghs.remedy: Then... who was the Nanaka I'd been seeing?

highlights.text: what is the Nanaka that I have been seeing?

rows.jp: まさか―――
rows.en: Could it be―――

ghs.en: No way---

rows.jp: ……よそう。
rows.en: ……No. Better not.

ghs.en: ...let's stop here.

rows.jp: 七香は無条件に俺の味方でいてくれた。
rows.en: Nanaka was on my side, unconditionally.

ghs.en: Nanaka has been, to me, an unconditional ally.

rows.jp: きっといつも、記憶の底から見守っていてくれたんだ。
rows.en: Surely she had always been watching over me from the depths of my memory.

ghs.en: She has always been watching over me from the bottom of my recollections, definitely.
ghs.assessment: 記憶の底 is the depths of memory, not the bottom of plural recollections. きっと expresses hopeful conviction in context; sentence-final 'definitely' sounds like an external factual certification.
ghs.remedy: from the depths of my memory, I'm sure

highlights.text: from the bottom of my recollections, definitely

rows.jp: そう思おう。
rows.en: That's what I'll believe.

ghs.en: I want to think that.

rows.jp: 事実は、世界が知っていればいい。
rows.en: The world can know the truth.

ghs.en: The world can go know the truth.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese means that it is enough for the world itself to know the facts. The English combines 'can go' and bare 'know' into an ungrammatical imperative-like phrase.
ghs.remedy: It's enough for the world to know the truth.

highlights.text: The world can go know the truth.

rows.jp: 俺が知る必要はない。
rows.en: I don't need to know.

ghs.en: I have no need to know.

rows.jp: 愛していてくれただけで、俺には―――充分すぎる。
rows.en: That she loved me is―――more than enough.

ghs.en: Merely having been loved, to me, it's--- more than plenty.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that simply knowing she loved him is more than enough for him. The English uses a dangling passive gerund, then repeats the experiencer as both 'to me' and the unexplained pronoun 'it.'
ghs.remedy: Just knowing she loved me is more than enough.

highlights.text: Merely having been loved, to me, it's--- more than plenty.

rows.jp: 涙を取り戻すと、次は認識が来た。
rows.en: Once I could cry again, realization followed.

ghs.en: And with the regainment of tears, next came the recognition.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that once his tears returned, realization followed. 'Regainment' is an awkward nominalization and the article before abstract 'recognition' does not establish a specific prior referent.
ghs.remedy: once my tears returned, realization followed

highlights.text: with the regainment of tears, next came the recognition

rows.jp: 人はただ、いてくれるだけでいい。
rows.en: Just having someone there is enough.

ghs.en: If people merely are... there, that's enough.

rows.jp: 場所も、性質も、性別も、問わない。
rows.en: Where they are, what they are like, what sex they are—it does not matter.

ghs.en: Their place, their nature, their gender, it does not matter.

rows.jp: いてほしいんだ。
rows.en: I want them to be there.

ghs.en: It's a want for them to be there.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese directly says 'I want them to be there.' The English converts the verb into a count noun governed by an expletive construction that is not idiomatic English.
ghs.remedy: I want them to be there.

highlights.text: It's a want for them to be there.

rows.jp: 人は人にいてほしい。
rows.en: People want someone else to be there.

ghs.en: People want people to be there.

rows.jp: より近くに、感じたい。
rows.en: They want to feel another person close.

ghs.en: They want to feel them nearer.

rows.jp: 手を伸ばした先に、誰かがいるという安心。
rows.en: The comfort of knowing that when you reach out, someone is there.

ghs.en: To be reassured that someone will be there even before they extend their hands.
ghs.assessment: 手を伸ばした先 means at the point reached by an outstretched hand. The English reverses the timing, placing the person there before the hand is extended at all.
ghs.remedy: someone is there within reach when they stretch out a hand

highlights.text: someone will be there even before they extend their hands

rows.jp: それを得たい。
rows.en: I want that.

ghs.en: That is what they want to obtain.

rows.jp: だから人は呼びかける。
rows.en: That is why people call out.

ghs.en: And therefore, people call out:

rows.jp: 電話で。言葉で。手紙で。態度で。
rows.en: By phone. By words. By letters. By actions.

ghs.en: with telephone, with words, with letters, with behavior.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese lists means of reaching out. English requires 'by phone' and idiomatic parallel prepositional phrases rather than repeated instrument-like 'with' and bare singular 'telephone.'
ghs.remedy: by phone, through words, in letters, through actions

highlights.text: with telephone, with words, with letters, with behavior

rows.jp: ……無線で。
rows.en: ……By radio.

ghs.en: ...with the radio.

rows.jp: どこかで誰かが聞いてくれますように。
rows.en: May someone, somewhere, hear.

ghs.en: So that they can get someone somewhere to listen.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese voices the hope that someone somewhere will hear the call. The English makes callers causatively 'get' a listener to perform an action and turns the wish into a purpose clause.
ghs.remedy: Hoping that someone, somewhere, will hear.

highlights.text: So that they can get someone somewhere to listen.

rows.jp: そう願って。
rows.en: That is the hope.

ghs.en: That is their wish.

rows.jp: みみ先輩は正しかった。
rows.en: Mimi was right.

ghs.en: Mimi-senpai was right.

rows.jp: 逃避だけど正しかった。
rows.en: It was an escape, but she was right.

ghs.en: She was running but she was right.
ghs.assessment: 逃避 means escape or escapism in the psychological sense. The English literalizes it as the physical act of running and adds a personal subject absent from the fragment.
ghs.remedy: It was escapism, but she was right.

highlights.text: She was running but she was right.

rows.jp: 俺は人なんだ。
rows.en: I'm human.

ghs.en: And so I am a person.

rows.jp: ああ。
rows.en: Yes.

ghs.en: Ahhh.

rows.jp: 信じられない。
rows.en: Unbelievable.

ghs.en: I can't believe this.

rows.jp: 深い意識にかき乱され、無邪気に人を壊してしまう俺だ。
rows.en: The depths of my consciousness churn me up, and I destroy people without even meaning to.

ghs.en: Disturbed by my deep consciousness, I've been innocent-mindedly destroying humans, that's what.
ghs.assessment: The source says that his deep consciousness churns him up and that he innocently destroys people. 'Innocent-mindedly' is not idiomatic, 'humans' is clinical in this reflection, and the present perfect progressive plus trailing 'that's what' replaces the source's characterization of himself.
ghs.remedy: I am someone whose deepest consciousness churns him up until he innocently destroys people.

highlights.text: Disturbed by my deep consciousness, I've been innocent-mindedly destroying humans, that's what.

rows.jp: 協調を衝動に阻害されるのだから、当然だ。
rows.en: Of course I struggle to cooperate when impulse gets in the way.

ghs.en: Seeing as my urge to cooperate was being obstructed by impulse, that'd be obvious.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that impulse obstructs his capacity for cooperation or harmony. The English instead invents a cooperative urge and makes a separate impulse obstruct that urge.
ghs.remedy: my ability to live in harmony is obstructed by my impulses

highlights.text: my urge to cooperate was being obstructed by impulse

rows.jp: けれど俺は、人だったんだ。
rows.en: But I was human after all.

ghs.en: And yet I... was a person.

rows.jp: 生きられる。
rows.en: I can live.

ghs.en: I can live.

rows.jp: その充足感で、俺は生きていける。
rows.en: That fulfillment is enough to keep me alive.

ghs.en: And I will live with that sense of fulfillment.

rows.jp: ゲートが消えて、世界は変わっていくかも知れない。
rows.en: With the gate gone, the world may begin to change.

ghs.en: So the gate may disappear, and the world may change, perhaps.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that the gate has disappeared and that the world may now change. The English makes the disappearance itself a future possibility.
ghs.remedy: the gate is gone

rows.jp: ここは交差点。
rows.en: This is the cross-point.

ghs.en: This is a Cross Point.

rows.jp: 過ぎ去れば、残像だけが美しい。
rows.en: Once it passes, only the afterimage is beautiful.

ghs.en: If it becomes past, then its afterimage alone will be what is beautiful.

rows.jp: 幻となって消えていく時が、来ているのだ。
rows.en: The time is coming for it to fade away as an illusion.

ghs.en: The time will come when it will become an illusion and disappear.
ghs.assessment: 時が来ている says that the time is already approaching or has come, not merely that it will arrive at some unspecified future point.
ghs.remedy: The time is coming

rows.jp: それはあとどれくらいなんだろう？
rows.en: How much longer will that be?

ghs.en: How far ahead will that be?

rows.jp: 来週か？
rows.en: Next week?

ghs.en: Next week maybe?

rows.jp: 再来週か？
rows.en: The week after?

ghs.en: The week after that maybe?

rows.jp: 来年か？
rows.en: Next year?

ghs.en: Next year, maybe?

rows.jp: ……俺が死ぬのと、どっちが早い？
rows.en: ……Which will come first: that, or my death?

ghs.en: ...and between that and my death, which will come first?

rows.jp: 死ぬわけにはいかない。
rows.en: I can't die.

ghs.en: Dying is out of the question,

rows.jp: 死ねばこのかけがえのない気持ちは、砕けてしまうから。
rows.en: Because if I die, this irreplaceable feeling will shatter.

ghs.en: for if I die, this irreplaceable feeling would be crushed into dust.

rows.jp: 「……生きてやる」
rows.en: “……I'll live.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...I'm gonna live."

rows.jp: 生き闘う。
rows.en: I will live and fight.

ghs.en: I will struggle to live.

rows.jp: 最後の日まで。
rows.en: Until the final day.

ghs.en: Until that very last day.

rows.jp: そして願う。
rows.en: And I make a wish.

ghs.en: And then I will wish,

rows.jp: 俺が固有の寿命を終える前に、どうか。
rows.en: Please, before I reach the end of my own natural life.

ghs.en: I will wish that before my eigenlifespan ends, somehow,
ghs.assessment: 固有の寿命 means his own allotted or natural lifespan. The English invents the technical compound 'eigenlifespan,' which has no established meaning in English.
ghs.remedy: my own lifespan

rows.jp: この空が消えてなくなりますようにと。
rows.en: May this sky vanish without a trace.

ghs.en: for the sky itself to finally pass away.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese wishes for the sky to disappear completely. 'Pass away' personifies it as dying and does not carry なくなる's complete disappearance, while 'finally' is added.
ghs.remedy: for this sky to disappear completely

highlights.text: the sky itself to finally pass away

rows.jp: 七香が微笑んでいる。
rows.en: Nanaka is smiling.

ghs.en: Nanaka is smiling.

rows.jp: 「ごめんね……それだけしか残してあげられなくて……」
rows.en: “I'm sorry... this is all I can leave you with...”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Sorry... I could leave you with nothing more than that..."

rows.jp: 残されたのは、世界でもっとも陳腐な部類の漢字一文字の単語と、生涯を通してありがちな人への渇望だった。
rows.en: What she left me was one of the tritest single-kanji words in the world, and a commonplace lifelong thirst for other people.

ghs.en: What she left me was a string of characters comprised of the world's most extreme cliche'-class words, and a craving to move throughout the course of my entire life towards being an ordinary person.
ghs.assessment: The source says she left him one single-kanji word of the most commonplace kind and a lifelong, ordinary longing for other people. The English turns one character into a string made of multiple words, adds 'most extreme,' and changes longing for people into a project of becoming an ordinary person.
ghs.remedy: a single-kanji word among the most commonplace in the world, and the ordinary longing for other people that would remain with me throughout my life

highlights.text: a string of characters comprised of the world's most extreme cliche'-class words, and a craving to move throughout the course of my entire life towards being an ordinary person

rows.jp: 俺は言った。
rows.en: I said.

ghs.en: And I told her,

rows.jp: 「ありがとう。もう、平気」
rows.en: “Thank you. I'm all right now.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Thank you. I'm alright now."

rows.jp: 七香は応じた。
rows.en: Nanaka answered.

ghs.en: Nanaka replied,

rows.en: “……Yeah!”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "...OK!"

rows.jp: 満面の、祝福の笑みだった。
rows.en: Her face was radiant with a smile of benediction.

ghs.en: It was an ear-to-ear full face smile of blessing.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese describes a beaming smile of blessing across her whole face. The English stacks two competing descriptions of width, uses 'full face' without the required hyphenation or idiomatic construction, and makes blessing an awkward postmodifier.
ghs.remedy: a radiant, full-faced smile of blessing

highlights.text: an ear-to-ear full face smile of blessing

rows.jp: そして七香を正しく認識すると同時に。
rows.en: And the moment I recognized Nanaka for what she was.

ghs.en: And then, simultaneously with my correct understanding of Nanaka,
ghs.assessment: 正しく認識する means to recognize or perceive Nanaka correctly in terms of what she is. 'Understanding of Nanaka' instead suggests a general intellectual or empathetic comprehension of her as a person.
ghs.remedy: recognizing Nanaka for what she was

rows.jp: 心は超越的な静穏を獲得した。
rows.en: My mind attained a transcendent calm.

ghs.en: my heart gained a transcendental serenity.
Taichi: "..."

rows.jp: 一人、立っていた。
rows.en: I stood alone.

ghs.en: I stood there, alone.

rows.jp: 林の中、俺という存在が、ひとつっきり。
rows.en: In the woods, there was one single existence: me.

ghs.en: In the heart of that grove, the only one thing remaining was this being, this being called me.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that within the grove there was only one existence: Taichi himself. The English uses the ungrammatical quantifier sequence 'only one thing,' adds that he was 'remaining,' and repeats 'this being' in inflated explanatory prose.
ghs.remedy: there was only one existence: me

highlights.text: the only one thing remaining was this being, this being called me

rows.jp: 静かだった。
rows.en: It was quiet.

ghs.en: It was silent.

rows.jp: 今まで体験したことのないほど。
rows.en: Quieter than I had ever known.

ghs.en: To a level that I had never experienced before in my life.

rows.jp: 「……衝動が……消えた……？」
rows.en: “……The impulse……is gone……?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...the impulse... is gone...?"

rows.jp: 俺を制御不能に陥らせる強烈な心の動きが、消失している。
rows.en: The violent surges of emotion that sent me out of control are gone.

ghs.en: The violent stirring of my heart which pushed me out of control had... disappeared.

rows.jp: 静かすぎて体内の物音さえ聞き取れそうで。
rows.en: It is so quiet I can almost hear the sounds inside my own body.

ghs.en: It seemed so excessively quiet that even the sounds inside the body could be heard.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese refers specifically to sounds inside Taichi's own body. The English shifts to a detached generic body.
ghs.remedy: the sounds inside my own body

rows.jp: 不安になる。
rows.en: I grow uneasy.

ghs.en: I become anxious.

rows.jp: 今まで心象風景の暴君だった、強烈なエゴが感じられない。
rows.en: I cannot feel the ferocious ego that had ruled the landscape of my mind like a tyrant.

ghs.en: I could no longer feel the violent ego that until now has been the tyrant of the imaginary landscape in my mind's eye.
ghs.assessment: The matrix verb is past while the relative clause uses present perfect with 'until now.' The surrounding realization requires a consistent current-perfect relation or a consistently narrated past one.
ghs.remedy: I could no longer feel the violent ego that until then had been

highlights.text: I could no longer feel the violent ego that until now has been

rows.jp: 本当に平穏は訪れたのか。
rows.en: Has peace truly come?

ghs.en: Did peacefulness really come to me,

rows.jp: 一時の夢なのか。
rows.en: Or is it a momentary dream?

ghs.en: or is this but a moment's dream?

rows.jp: 心細い。
rows.en: I feel lost.

ghs.en: Discouragement.
ghs.assessment: 心細い expresses feeling uneasy, insecure, or forlorn because support is absent. 'Discouragement' instead means a loss of confidence or enthusiasm after difficulty.
